turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Let's listen to the teacher reading the story.
turns.en: Let's listen to the teacher reading the story.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Okay. Ngizofunda indaba. Indaba yethu ithi...
turns.en: Okay. I am going to read the story. Our story says...

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: In our lesson of today of reading aloud,

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: sizofunda indaba yethu emnandi kakhulu bafundi.
turns.en: we are going to read our very nice story, learners.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Indaba esesizoyifunda namhlanje isihloko sayo sithi, umlimi nehashi lakhe.
turns.en: The story that we are going to read today, its title says, the farmer and their horse.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Imnandi kakhulu lendaba esizobe siyifunda namhlanje futhi kuningi esingakufunda nje ngempilo nje singabantu.
turns.en: It is very nice, this story that we will be reading today, and there is a lot we can learn just about life as people.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Uma ngabe uzwa isihloko esithi umlimi nehashi lakhe, yini efikayo kuwena? Ucabanga ukuthi le ndaba izobe ikhuluma ngani?
turns.en: If you hear the title that says the farmer and their horse, what comes to you? What do you think this story will be talking about?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Umlimi nehashi lakhe basebenza ubusuku nemini engadini.
turns.en: The farmer and their horse work night and day in the garden.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ake siqhubekeleni phambili ke ke. Uma ngabe sizwa isihloko sithi umlimi nehashi lakhe, yini kanti umlimi? Sesake sambona thina umlimi empilweni yethu?
turns.en: Let us move forward then. If we hear the title saying the farmer and their horse, what is a farmer anyway? Have we ever seen a farmer in our lives?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.en: A farmer is a person who works in the garden.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Okay, very good. Sesizwile ukuthi isihloko besikhuluma ngani? Ngomlimi. Siphinde futhi sesikhuluma ngani? Nangehhashi.
turns.en: Okay, very good. We have heard what the title was talking about? About the farmer. And again, what is it talking about? And about the horse.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ubongasichazela ukuthi masikhuluma ngehhashi kusuke kukhulunywa ngani? [learner]?
turns.en: Could you explain to us, when we talk about a horse, what is being talked about? [learner]?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Ihhashi isilwane esinemilenze emine futhi siyakwazi ukugibelwa abantu.
turns.en: A horse is an animal that has four legs and it can be ridden by people.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Very good. Sithe isihloko sendaba yethu ithi umlimi nehhashi lakhe.
turns.en: Very good. We said the title of our story says the farmer and their horse.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Lalelani ke. Indaba yethu ethi uMlimi nehashi lakhe ikhuluma ngomnumzane Dlamini.
turns.en: Listen then. Our story that says the Farmer and their horse talks about Mr Dlamini.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Niyezwa? Owayenendodana yakhe eyodwa vo, ogama layo kwakubani? UZolani.
turns.en: Do you hear? Who had their only son, whose name was who? Zolani.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Bathi ngaphambi kokuba siyofunda indaba, kunamagama amasha asendabeni okumele kuqale sidlule kuwona siwachaze ukuthi ingabe achaza ukuthini.
turns.en: They say before we go to read the story, there are new words in the story that we must first go through and explain what they mean.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ubani ongangifundela leli gama? Lithini leli gama? Phakamisa isandla sakho.
turns.en: Who can read this word for me? What does this word say? Raise your hand.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Isiphi isithombe othi wena sihambisana naleli gama elithi qhubha?
turns.en: Which picture do you say goes with this word that says qhubha?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: Let us clap hands for [learner] as they sit down.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Igama elithi lithi qhubha lisho ukuthini?
turns.en: The word that says qhubha means what?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Asenzeni sonke ke siqhubhe, senjani mangabe siqhubha? Qhubha.
turns.en: Let us all do then we drive, what do we do when we drive? Drive.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Okay, asilaleleni ke. Ukuqhuba ukuhambisa into ngaphambi kwakho ubuyiqondise ukuthi ayibheke ngakhephi.
turns.en: Okay, let us listen then. To drive is to move something in front of you and direct it where it should look.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Uzothatha igama elithi qhuba bese akhande umusho ngalo.
turns.en: Who will take the word qhuba and then make a sentence with it?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ingabe leli gama singalibeka singalisebenzisa kanjani emshweni?
turns.en: How can we put this word, how can we use it in a sentence?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Okay, asilaleleni ke manje. Siyadlulela, sidlulele egameni lethu lesibili.
turns.en: Okay, let us listen now. We are passing, we pass to our second word.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ubani ongangichazela igama lami leli lesibili?
turns.en: Who can explain to me this second word of mine?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: What is the word? Let us all read.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ukuhlakula ukwenzenjani ke? Asenzeni sonke. Mangabe sihlakula senzenjani? Siphethe amageja senzenjani? Siyahlakula. Senzenjani?
turns.en: To weed is to do what then? Let us all do. When we weed what do we do? We hold hoes and do what? We are weeding. What do we do?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Okay, ngaphambi kokuthi silichaze igama ukuthi lisho ukuthini, isiphi isithombe esihambisana naleli gama?
turns.en: Okay, before we explain what the word means, which picture goes with this word?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Isiphi isithombe esihambisana naleli gama elithi hlakula?
turns.en: Which picture goes with this word that says weed?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: Is the picture held by [learner] right?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: Why? What is this person doing then?

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Igama elithi sihlakula likhaza ukuthini? Lisho ukuthini nje?
turns.en: The word that says we weed, what does it mean? What does it just mean?

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.en: To weed is to weed in the soil.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.en: Okay, you say to weed is to weed the-

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: ukuthi ukuhlakula kuyini. Ukuhlakula ukukhipha ukhula kephi ezitshalweni.
turns.en: what weeding is. Weeding is to remove weeds where, from the plants.

turns.speaker: Teacher
turns.text: Ngizocela umuntu oyedwa ke eqenjini ngalinye eze ngaphambili.
turns.en: I will ask one person then from each group to come to the front.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Abushelelezi, ubucwacwacwa, bengazelele, ucwezu, acebile, xotshisa amatshe, ufeleba, gudla, hwehwa, uhlanzi, ohlangothini, ihlo, ihlozi, imvukuzane, amahlengethwa, mpunga, qoloda, ukushintsha, tshatha, izimpophomo.
turns.en: Smooth, glitter, unexpectedly, slice, they are rich, skip stones, giant, scrape, beckon, clean, on the side, eye, leopard, mole, dolphins, grey, leap, to change, carry on shoulders, waterfalls.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Izimpophoma, izingwadule, imbazo, matasatasa, imizuzu, ingqina, shosholoza, izi-
turns.en: Waterfalls, deserts, axe, busy, minutes, steenbok, push forward, izi-

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: imizuzu, inyembe, shosholoza, isigidi, izintsa- izintsalela, amathambo, igaduni, umfomuko, khuculula, isikhukhuka, isikhukhumalisi samubumbana, isizemazema, ihlamvu, intsempe, mbibi, isiminsi sinenhlanhla esiyisizemazema, yisilande yisilandlekazi.
turns.en: minutes, tear, push forward, million, rem- remains, bones, garden, overflow, clean up, flood, baking powder of clay, giant, leaf, partridge, striped mouse, the lucky glutton which is a giant, it is a long story/giant woman.

turns.speaker: Learner
turns.text: Tholihlala, ithinga, isimizi, ibhulohwe, hlakula, khuba.
turns.en: Tholihlala, ithinga, isimizi, bridge, weed, hoe.
